dbbfe8: Place \(m\) \(1 \times 2\) dominos on a \(7\times7\) chessboard such that no domino can slide horizontally or vertically when other dominos remains fixed. Find the minimal possible value of \(m\).
a824c1: How many squares at least should be marked on a \(13\times13\) chessboard such that for any placement of a bishop on the chessboard, the bishop can threaten at least one of the marked squares? (A bishop can threaten the squares on the same diagonal line, and if a bishop is placed on a marked square, it is also considered that the square is threatened.)
673b29: An explorer is challenging to pass through a maze composed of 3033 rows and 3032 columns of squares. The rules of the maze are as follows: In all the middle rows (that is, from the 2nd row to the 3032nd row), there is one invisible teleportation gate hidden in each row, and there are no multiple invisible teleportation gates in the same column. The explorer starts from any position in the 1st row. Each time, he can move one square up, down, left or right, and it is allowed to pass through the explored areas repeatedly. If the explorer touches a teleportation gate, he will immediately return to the starting point and start the next attempt. However, the explorer will mark the position of that teleportation gate. If the explorer reaches any position in the 3033rd row, he will directly pass the maze. It is known that the explorer can remember the positions of all the discovered teleportation gates. Please construct a general strategy so that no matter how the teleportation gates are distributed, the explorer will definitely pass the maze in the \(k\)th attempt in the worst-case scenario. Find the minimum possible value of \(k\).
414a5b: Kevin throws three fair dice numbered from 1 to 6. Then he observes the results of the first throw of the three dice. From these three dice, he can choose \(n\), where \(0\leq n\leq3\) dice to re-throw once. After that, the operation ends. Kevin's goal is to maximize the probability that the sum of the numbers on the final three dice is 7, and Kevin is smart enough. Let the probability when \(n = 2\) be \(p\). What is the value of \(216\times p\)?
a9dbc8: The Bank of Pittsburgh issues coins that have a heads side and a tails side. Vera has a row of 7873 such coins alternately tails-up and heads-up, with the leftmost coin tails-up. In a move, Vera may flip over one of the coins in the row, subject to the following rules: • On the first move, Vera may flip over any of the 7873 coins. • On all subsequent moves, Vera may only flip over a coin adjacent to the coin she flipped on the previous move. (We do not consider a coin to be adjacent to itself.) Determine the smallest possible number of moves Vera can make to reach a state in which every coin is heads-up.
9010d9: Let \(G\) be a 160-order simple graph. For any vertex \(u\), there exists another vertex \(v\), such that \(u\) and \(v\) are adjacent, and there exists no vertices adjacent to both \(u\) and \(v\). Find the maximal number of edges in \(G\).
